name: xdg-defaults
description: How a default application is read and set on this desktop: which xdg-settings properties exist, which xdg-mime operations exist, which file each one writes, and what the Startup & Default apps page may therefore offer. A default the tools cannot set is recorded as unsettable rather than offered as a switch that silently does nothing.
verified_against: xdg-utils scripts/xdg-settings.in and scripts/xdg-mime.in at freedesktop-unofficial-mirror/xdg__xdg-utils master c5512229 (committed 2015-04-13); glib 2.84.4 gio/gdesktopappinfo.c, both fetched 2026-11-13
source: scripts/xdg-settings.in (dispatch_specific :633-692, dispatch_generic :694-712, get_browser_mime :108-118, set_browser_mime :119-137) and scripts/xdg-mime.in (the argument dispatch :440-528, make_default_generic :242-301, defapp_generic :346-395) in freedesktop-unofficial-mirror/xdg__xdg-utils at c5512229; gio/gdesktopappinfo.c (the desktop-file loader :1898-1980, should_show :3688-3696, get_all_for_type :4547-4569, the mimeapps.list tweaks :896-975) in GNOME/glib at 2.84.4
_note: The official xdg-utils repository is on gitlab.freedesktop.org, which this sandbox cannot reach; the mirror cited is unofficial and its last commit is from 2015, so what is verified here is that snapshot of the two scripts and not the release a distribution ships today. docs/UNVERIFIED.md SET-08 records exactly that limitation. The consequences below are all of the conservative kind -- they say what the tools refuse to do rather than what they are newly able to do -- so a newer release can only widen what is offered, never invalidate a refusal recorded here.

properties.argument: one .desktop file name, checked with check_desktop_filename before it is used
properties.meaning: The default handler for text/html. get_browser_mime and set_browser_mime default to that mimetype when none is given, so 'the browser' is one MIME association and not a separate setting.
properties.evidence: scripts/xdg-settings.in:641-643, :655-658, :669-673 and the default MIME at :108-118

properties.argument: a scheme name, then one .desktop file name for check and set
properties.meaning: The default handler for x-scheme-handler/<scheme>, which is how a mailto: or a webcal: link is routed.

refusals.behaviour: exit_failure_syntax when a desktop environment was detected (:650-651, :664-665, :682-683), and exit_failure_operation_impossible in the generic path (:699-700)
refusals.why_it_matters: There is no xdg-settings property for a terminal emulator, a file manager or a text editor. A page offering 'default terminal' through this tool would be offering a command that exits with a failure, so those three are set through xdg-mime's MIME associations instead -- or, for a terminal, not at all: see unsettable.

refusals.what: Any operation other than get or check, when no desktop environment was detected
refusals.behaviour: dispatch_generic refuses with exit_failure_operation_impossible, and additionally refuses any property that is not default-web-browser (:697-700)
refusals.why_it_matters: This session's XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP is not GNOME, KDE or XFCE, so the generic path is the one that runs. `xdg-settings set default-web-browser` is therefore not a mechanism this project can rely on: the write it performs is xdg-mime's, reached through set_browser_mime (:119-137), and that is what this project calls directly instead.

operations.prints: the .desktop file name associated with that mimetype, or nothing
operations.refuses: a mimetype with no '/' in it: exit_failure_syntax "mimetype '$mimetype' is not in the form 'minor/major'"

operations.prints: the mimetype of an existing file
operations.refuses: a missing argument, or a filename beginning with '-'
a first argument that does not end in .desktop: exit_failure_syntax "malformed argument '$1', expected *.desktop"
operations.evidence: scripts/xdg-mime.in:500-520 for the argument check, :530-545 for the dispatch, and make_default_generic :242-301 for the file it writes
operations.note: The file written is under XDG_DATA_HOME, not XDG_CONFIG_HOME. A page that reported the change as living in ~/.config/mimeapps.list would be pointing at a file nothing wrote.

operations.writes: a .desktop file into the applications directories, plus the KDE 3 vendor files it maintains
operations.why_not: Installing an application is not a settings page's job, and the uninstall branch removes files by name from every XDG data directory -- a delete this project will not perform on a file it did not create.

read_order.description: Where `query default` looks, in order. The user's own file wins, which is what makes a change made here survive a system package update.
paths: each directory of $XDG_DATA_DIRS (default /usr/local/share/:/usr/share/), same two file names

verify_and_restore.description: set_browser_mime reads the association back after writing it and, when the read-back does not equal what was asked for, writes the original value again.
verify_and_restore.why_it_matters: Upstream already treats a default-application write as something that has to be verified rather than assumed, and rolls back when it fails. The apply pipeline in iarch/settings-app does the same thing for every file it writes, so the two agree on what 'applied' means.

roles.label: Web browser
roles.why: text/html is the association xdg-settings itself means by 'default web browser' (:108-118), and the two scheme handlers are what a link clicked outside a browser resolves through. Setting all three is what stops a page opening in one program and a link in another.

roles.label: File manager
roles.why: inode/directory is the association a file manager is reached through. The second mimetype is there because this repository's own installers already set both for Thunar in one command (install.sh:1245, fedora_install.sh:897): writing only the first would leave saved searches pointing at whatever the install chose, so the page and the installer would disagree about the same role.
roles.evidence: install.sh:1245 and fedora_install.sh:897 (both `xdg-mime default thunar.desktop inode/directory application/x-gnome-saved-search`); fedora_install.sh:1102 sets inode/directory alone

roles.label: Text editor
roles.why: text/plain is the association a plain text file resolves through. It is one mimetype and not a list of every text format, because a page that offered to claim forty mimetypes would be claiming file types the user did not ask about.
roles.evidence: scripts/xdg-mime.in:500-520 (any mimetype list is accepted; this project sends one)

roles.label: Mail client
roles.why: The Contact page opens mailto: links through Gio.AppInfo.launch_default_for_uri, which resolves through this association. Setting it is what makes that button reach a mail client rather than failing silently.
roles.evidence: scripts/xdg-settings.in:493-496 and :526 (the scheme-handler property is the same association under a different name)

candidates._note: Which programs a role's dropdown may offer, and why each one is in or out. Read out of glib because glib is what every application chooser on this desktop uses, so a list that disagreed with it would offer a program the rest of the desktop hides or hide one it offers.
candidates.how: The page reads the .desktop files in the application directories and keeps the ones whose MimeType line names one of the role's mimetypes. It does not call Gio: the page has to be testable with no display server and no PyGObject installed, and scanning the same directories answers the same question with a citation behind every filter.
directories: each directory of $XDG_DATA_DIRS with /applications appended; the default for that variable is /usr/local/share/:/usr/share/
candidates.directories_evidence: scripts/xdg-mime.in:346-395 (defapp_generic reads exactly these, in this order) and gio/gdesktopappinfo.c:1180-1200 (glib indexes the same files)

filters.why: glib does not index a Hidden desktop file at all, so a program that hid itself this way would appear in this list and nowhere else on the desktop.
Gio.AppInfo.should_show is false when NoDisplay is true, and that is the test every application chooser applies before offering a program.

filters.keep_when: it is absent, or names a program that can be found
filters.why: glib refuses to load the file at all when TryExec cannot be resolved, which is how a desktop file says the program is not installed.

filters.keep_when: it is present and can be parsed as a command line
filters.why: glib refuses to load a file whose Exec line it cannot parse, and a file with no Exec line cannot launch anything.

filters.keep_when: it names at least one of the role's mimetypes
filters.why: That line is the program's own claim about what it can open. A program that does not claim the type is not offered for it, because choosing it would ask a program to open something it never said it could.
filters.evidence: gio/gdesktopappinfo.c:1975 (MimeType is read into the program's type list) and :4547-4569 (the answer for a type comes from that list)

filters.keep_when: it is present in some language
filters.why: A row with no label is a row nobody can choose.

always_listed.what: The association that is currently set, even when its own file would be filtered out by one of the rules above.
always_listed.why: A dropdown that cannot show the value already in force looks unset and invites a pointless change. The row is marked, so a person can see that the program no longer claims the type, or is no longer installed, rather than wondering why it is there.
always_listed.evidence: scripts/xdg-mime.in:346-395 (query default answers with a file name whether or not that file still claims the type)

localised_names.what: Name, GenericName, Comment and Keywords are read with the locale in brackets first and the unlocalised key as the fallback, so a candidate's label is shown in the user's language.
localised_names.why: This is the opposite of the autostart generator, where a key with a bracket in it is ignored: the same file format has two readers and they do not agree. data/design/autostart.json records the other half, and the difference is why a startup entry this project writes carries one unlocalised Name while a candidate here may carry several.

limitation.what: glib also applies the [Added Associations] and [Removed Associations] groups of mimeapps.list when it answers which programs handle a type. This scan does not.
limitation.consequence: A program associated with a type only through one of those groups is not offered as a candidate. It is still shown when it is the current default, because of always_listed. The error is in the direction of offering less rather than more, which is the direction this project prefers to be wrong in.

unsettable.label: Terminal emulator
unsettable.why: There is no xdg-settings property for one (:699-700 refuses anything but the two recorded properties) and no MIME type that means 'open a terminal here', so there is no standard association to write. Which terminal a keyboard shortcut launches is decided by this session's own binds in .config/hypr/keybind.lua and by the shell's launcher, and both are configured elsewhere in this project. The page says that instead of offering a dropdown that would write a file nothing reads.

unsettable.role: any role, when neither tool is installed
unsettable.why: xdg-mime and xdg-settings come from xdg-utils, which neither installer in this repository adds to its package list. A missing binary is unverified rather than a failure, so the page shows what it could not read and does not offer a write it cannot verify afterwards.
